entries.title: Proverbs 26:2
segments: As the bird by wandering--so the curse causeless shall not come; God's curse will not come upon men at random, like the flight of birds.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:4
segments:
Answer not a fool according to his folly; with such foolish words as he uses. 
 
vv 4-5. In dealing with the ignorant and self-conceited, great wisdom is necessary, lest, on the one side, we make ourselves like them, or, on the other, fail to put to silence their foolish words.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:5
segments: Answer a fool according to his folly; in a manner adapted to rebuke it.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:6
segments: Cutteth off the feet; his own feet, and thus cripples himself in respect to the business on hand.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:7
segments:
Are not equal; so that he has a limping gait.  Others render, "hang down;" that is, as a useless weight. 
 
  So is a parable in the mouth of fools; they have not skill to make a discreet use of it.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:8
segments:
Bindeth a stone in a sling; performs an absurd and useless act. Or, "Putteth a precious stone in a heap of stones," among which it will be lost. 
 
All preferment is thrown away upon the foolish.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:9
segments:
Into the hand of a drunkard; a reeling drunkard, who lays hold of it to support himself. 
 
  A parable in the mouth of fools; by perverting it, they make it an injury to themselves. 
 
It is the part of folly to pervert to its own injury that which was designed for its profit.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:16
segments:
A reason; a good reason for a wise course of action.  The sluggard's course is foolish and ruinous, yet he thinks himself wiser than all his advisers. 
 
They who have no good reason to give for their conduct, are most inclined to despise the counsels of the wise.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:17
segments:
By the ears; to his own hurt. 
 
Intermeddlers always bring themselves into trouble.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:19
segments: Falsehood and deception do not become either innocent or harmless because practised in sport; the deceiver who excuses himself on this ground, will find that at God's bar these are treated as heinous offences.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:20
segments: Since talebearers exist in every community, the best way is to rebuke them, and close our ears to their words.  Where the people have wisdom to do this, strife will cease.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:21
segments:
Coals--to burning coals; coals added to a heap of burning coals, which makes the fire hotter. 
 
The contentious man's tongue is "set on fire of hell;" and he sets on fire the whole community in which he dwells.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:23
segments:
Burning lips; his lips that make warm professions of love. 
 
  Silver dross; glittering, yet worthless.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:24
segments: vv 24-26. The weapons of malice are flattery, hypocrisy, and deceit, but God's providence will strip off its disguises and expose its wickedness before the world.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:27
segments:
Rolleth; in order that it may overwhelm others. 
 
  Return upon him; fall back upon him by the slipping of his hands. By some unforeseen turn of events, the mischief which he was preparing for others shall fall upon himself.
